concept.name: Crossed market
concept.definition: A market state in which the best bid exceeds the best offer, producing a negative displayed spread. Regulation NMS Rule 610(e) requires exchange rules that members reasonably avoid displaying quotations that cross protected quotations, and Rule 611(b)(4) excepts from trade-through liability executions occurring while a protected bid is priced higher than a protected offer.
concept.intuition: Someone is publicly bidding more than someone else is asking - arbitrage on its face, usually an artifact of timing rather than a real opportunity.
concept.mechanics: Crosses are typically transient states caused by latency and feed delays across fragmented venues during fast price moves; they resolve through quote reconciliation, routing, or cancellation, often within microseconds to seconds.
concept.failure_modes: A crossed consolidated quote usually reflects a stale or slow data feed rather than an executable arbitrage; attempting to trade the apparent cross generally finds the quote already gone.
concept.misconceptions: A crossed NBBO almost never means free money - the crossing quotation is typically stale, inaccessible, or already executed by faster participants.
concept.example: During a rapid sell-off the consolidated feed briefly shows NBB $100.03 and NBO $100.02; within a few hundred microseconds the stale offer is updated and the cross disappears.

citations.source: 17 CFR 242.610 - Access to quotations (Regulation NMS Rule 610)
